title: Extract's settle leaves a cancelled job's run mid-stage
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/extract.ts settleExtract copies only a FAILED kernel ending onto run.json; a cancelled job leaves the manifest reading a running stage with nobody driving it, where strips' settle handles failed AND cancelled.

## Description
settleExtract (lib/producers/extract.ts, early return unless job.state is failed) is the post-job hook the kernel runs after every drive. Its strips twin (lib/producers/strips.ts settleStripsRun) handles failed and cancelled and says why: a job the KERNEL ended - its ceiling, the breaker, a money stop, a cancel - never ran the step that tells the artefact store. For extract a cancel ends the job and run.json keeps `reading`/`replicating`, which v1's readers (the commit's done|failed gate, the Weir) read as live. Fixed looks like: a cancelled job's manifest is ended with its reason, without breaking launchExtract({ rerun: true }) of a cancelled run - that interaction is why this is not built unread.

## Flow
- launch an extract run, drive one unit, cancel the job -> settleExtract returns early -> run.json stays at its stage
- fix: settle cancelled like strips (status, error, log line) and let the rerun path revive a manifest ended by a cancel
- pin both in tests/next-server/producer-extract-job.test.ts

## Expected impact
The Weir and the extract commit stop showing a cancelled run as in progress. Could break: a rerun of a cancelled run if the revive path does not accept the new ending.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a kernel-ended extract job always leaves its manifest ended
Before: 1 of 2 settle hooks (strips) handles cancelled; extract's ignores it (read of both functions)
After: 2 of 2, and a cancelled run's rerun still drives
Method: simulation - walked the cancel path, the rerun path (target.rerun with held.state cancelled) and the commit gate; no driven case exists for an extract cancel
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/extract.ts settleExtract: if (job.producer !== "extract" || job.state !== "failed" || job.error === undefined) return;
lib/producers/strips.ts settleStripsRun: (job.state !== "failed" && job.state !== "cancelled")
instrument: a driven case in tests/next-server/producer-extract-job.test.ts: cancel mid-run -> run.json status; then rerun -> the ~2 job drives to done

title: The still and voice landings never write the records the domain declares for them
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/still.ts and voice.ts land return { rev: 0, unchanged: true }; the STILL record (takes as blob refs and the adopted one) and the VOICE record (takes and the active one per line) exist in @gt/domain/steps and nothing writes them.

## Description
The pair of the wave-3 words card (audio-text-producers: The words landing never writes the words record the domain declares for it). STEP_RECORDS carries still (packages/domain/src/steps/still.ts) and voice (parts.ts VOICE, with a refine that every byLine take id is held). The bindings book takes on the job only (unit:take:<n> outputs, voice blobs) and their comments now say so (d99f1e70). Fixed looks like: the landing appends each produced take to its record inside the job's fenced landing (landPart), so the gate packet and the mv still step can read the record rather than the job's outputs.

## Flow
- drive a dry still-takes job -> readPart(still) holds no takes
- fix: landPart writes { still: { ...rec, takes: [...rec.takes, ...booked] } }; voice likewise into takes/byLine
- a driven case per part

## Expected impact
The album still's takes and the explainer's voice takes become part records an editor and the cut can read. Could break: readers that read the job outputs today (the mv still step, cut) if they are switched in the same change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - takes land where the domain says they live
Before: 0 of 2 part kinds write their declared record (still, voice); words likewise (filed in wave 3)
After: 2 of 2, the job outputs unchanged
Method: simulation - walked still-takes and record-line; the record write's interaction with the gate packet and the parts driver's ownership rules is not measured
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/still.ts land: ok({ rev: 0, unchanged: true })
lib/producers/voice.ts land: ok({ rev: 0, unchanged: true })
packages/domain/src/steps/still.ts STILL; packages/domain/src/steps/parts.ts VOICE
instrument: driven cases in tests/next-server/producer-step-still.test.ts and producer-step-words-voice.test.ts reading the part record after a dry job

title: Article, strips and Suno read every job in the store to find one run's
body:
## Summary
articleJobsOf and heldRuns (lib/producers/article.ts), stripsJobs (strips.ts) and sunoKernelJobs (suno.ts) call list(store) - every job of every producer - and filter in memory; several callers want one job by a derived id.

## Description
The mv form of this was measured and fixed (6fe8069b: 16.30 -> 0.09 ms per lookup on a 3001-job store). In article.ts, enqueueAct checks one derived id through articleJobsOf, followMode finds the gate job by id the same way, resumeArticle finds one id, and loopDriver.driven scans per run. Fixed looks like: get(store, id) where one id is wanted, a SQL filter (producer, of id) where a run's jobs are wanted - list has no producer filter today, so that half may be the kernel's change (out of scope).

## Flow
- build a temp store with N jobs of other producers
- time articleJobsOf / enqueueAct / followMode before and after, asserting the same job
- switch the single-id call sites to get; leave the scans that want a set

## Expected impact
Article acts and the loop's per-run checks stop scaling with the whole store's job count. Could break: nothing if each replaced lookup returns the same job (the probe compares).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one-job lookups read one row
Before: articleJobsOf parses every job per call (5 call sites in article.ts); figure not taken this round
After: one row per single-id lookup
Method: simulation - the mv probe's shape applies; article.ts sits at 398 lines so the change must stay line-neutral
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/article.ts articleJobsOf: list(store) then filter (callers enqueueAct, followMode, reworkArticle, resumeArticle, loopDriver.driven)
lib/producers/strips.ts stripsJobs: list(store)
lib/producers/suno.ts sunoKernelJobs: list(store)
instrument: a probe like the round's scratchpad mv-lookup-probe.mts over articleJobsOf/enqueueAct on a 3000-job temp store, same answer asserted

title: Plates and look references are read from the process store's blobs, not the job's
body:
## Summary
cut.ts withPlates (blobRoot from storeLocation), motion.ts (blobRootOf(stepKernel().store)) and frames/still kernelBlobs read a plate's or reference's bytes from the PROCESS kernel's blob root, while the plate was written by ctx.fx.blob into the blob store of the effects the job is driven with.

## Description
driveStep(factory, store, jobId) builds effects over the job's own store (effectsOf(store)), so a plate a frames job lands is in <dir of that store>/blobs; the motion, cut and still bindings then read plates through the process's kernel (GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH or foundry-out). In the worker the two are one store; a door that drives a part job over a store it was handed (L52's pattern, the tests' temp kernels) reads the wrong directory - cut draws the plate as a gap, motion fails its must(read). The tests avoid it by also pointing GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH at their temp store. Fixed looks like: read through the job's own effects (a blob read on Effects, or the root derived from the job's store), the way publish.ts takes the store it is handed.

## Flow
- open a temp kernel A, set GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH to another path B
- land plates with a dry frames job on A, then drive export-animatic on A
- observe: the animatic draws every plate as a gap (bytes looked up under B's blobs)

## Expected impact
A part job driven over a handed store reads the plates it wrote. Could break: callers that rely on the process kernel opening lazily (frames/still kernelBlobs is a lazy default).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a part job reads plates from the store it runs on
Before: 3 bindings (cut, motion, frames/still references) read the process store's blobs; 0 read the job's
After: 3 of 3 read the store the job runs on
Method: simulation - walked driveStep -> effectsOf(store) writes vs cut.ts blobRoot() / motion store() / kernelBlobs reads; no case drives with the two stores apart
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/cut.ts blobRoot(): storeLocation(OUT_DIRNAME)
lib/producers/motion.ts motionProducer: blobs ?? blobStore(blobRootOf(stepKernel().store))
lib/producers/frames.ts kernelBlobs = blobStore(blobRootOf(stepKernel().store))
lib/producers/research.ts driveStep: fx = o.fx ?? effectsOf(store)
instrument: a driven case in tests/next-server/producer-step-cut.test.ts with GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH pointing away from the job's store: plates read as gaps before, drawn after

title: Five scout and mesh bindings still carry their own copy of jobOf
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/mesh.ts, scoutAsset.ts, scoutIdea.ts, scoutIngest.ts and scoutReel.ts each define the same jobOf(store, id) that forge.ts now exports for strips and extract (a8e4169a).

## Description
Same body in all five (parseAt job id, kernel get, not-found -> undefined, else throw). These files are another context's (not in bound-producers' file_paths), so this round collapsed only its own three copies. Fixed looks like: each imports jobOf from ./forge.ts and drops parseAt/jobIdSchema/get where they become unused.

## Flow
- grep -n 'function jobOf' lib/producers/*.ts -> 6 definitions (forge + 5)
- replace the five with imports
- run their tests (decision-v1-scout-*, mesh-cli, scout probes)

## Expected impact
One definition of a job lookup across the producer bindings. Could break: nothing if the bodies are identical (they are, by read).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of one rule
Before: 6 definitions of jobOf in lib/producers
After: 1
Method: probe - grep count; out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/producers/mesh.ts:43, scoutAsset.ts:142, scoutIdea.ts:148, scoutIngest.ts:53, scoutReel.ts:175: function jobOf(store: Store, id: string)
instrument: grep count plus the scout/mesh vitest files green

title: A voice stand-in take counts whitespace as words
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/voice.ts sizes a dry take by line.split(/\s+/).length / 2.5; a line with leading or trailing whitespace (linesIn filters on trim but passes the untrimmed text) counts the empty tokens as words.

## Description
linesIn keeps b.text as written and only drops lines whose trim is empty; perform then splits the raw line, so a 2-word line padded with spaces is 4 tokens (1.6 s) where it should be 1 s (the floor). The stand-in length is what cut lays the dry voice on. No case drives record-line with lines at all (producer-step-words-voice covers the refusal only). Fixed looks like: count line.trim().split(/\s+/).

## Flow
- seed a script render whose adopted beat text has surrounding spaces
- drive a dry record-line job
- read the booked seconds: 1.6 before, 1 after

## Expected impact
Dry voice takes are as long as their words. Could break: nothing (stand-in only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a stand-in take's length follows its words
Before: a padded 2-word line books 1.6 s (walked)
After: 1 s
Method: simulation - walked the split; no driven record-line case exists to take the figure
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/voice.ts perform: const seconds = Math.max(1, line.split(/\s+/).length / WORDS_PER_S);
linesIn: .filter((b) => b.text.trim() !== "").map((b) => ({ ..., text: b.text }))
instrument: a driven dry record-line case in tests/next-server/producer-step-words-voice.test.ts

title: The registry binds each step's lanes once, on the day the process imports it
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/registry.ts lanesOf(name) and styleLaunch.ts STYLE_LANE are computed at import with that day's catalog; the hypothesis was that a long-running worker misses a lane an option gains later.

## Description
modelOptions(kind, day) takes a day, so BOUND (computed once) could drift from what a later launch routes to. Measured: the day only picks PRICE rows; every option's key and lane come from the catalog declaration and the router table.

## Flow
- probe: every WORK_KIND's option key@lane signature on 2026-10-24, 2027-01-02 and 2027-12-31

## Expected impact
None - nothing to change.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the worker's bound lanes follow the day
Before: option@lane signature on 2026-10-24: 1715 chars
After: identical on 2027-01-02 and 2027-12-31
Method: probe - scratchpad lanes-probe.mts over modelOptions on three days
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: lanes-probe: 2026-10-24 same lanes 1715 / 2027-01-02 same lanes 1715 / 2027-12-31 same lanes 1715
